# Licensing status and DVLA lookups {#sec-dd-dvla-status}

```{r}
source("R/book.R")
cols <- dict_groups$dvla_status
cs <- coverage_share(cols)
dm <- read_pipeline("outputs", "quality", "dvla_match.csv")
dm_n <- tapply(dm$n_vehicles, dm$dvla_match, sum)
```

## Overview

DVLA details were collected by querying the Vehicle Enquiry Service (VES) for
every registration in the DVSA data, many of them several times, between 2024
and 2026 (@sec-sources-linkage). These columns hold the vehicle's licensing
status as the VES reported it, the record of the lookups themselves, and the
pipeline's check of whether the VES record describes the same vehicle.

- **Licensing status**: tax status and due date, MOT status and expiry,
  whether the vehicle is marked for export, the date of its latest V5C
  (registration certificate) and the end date of the additional rate of tax
  (the supplement for cars with a high list price), all as at the last lookup that returned a record. These are
  supplied by the DVLA and not changed. @sec-lifecycle explains SORN, export
  and the other stages they describe.
- **What changed between lookups**: `ever_SORN`, `ever_export_marked`,
  `plate_ever_changed_VES`, `v5C_issue_date_ever_changed` and
  `change_in_other_VES_field` summarise the changes seen
  across repeated lookups.
- **The lookups**: when the registration was first and last queried and first
  and last returned a record, how many queries were made, and the error from
  the last one where it failed (methodology,
  [section 2](../../reports/methodology.md#input-data)). `n_DVLA_makes`
  is the number of different makes the lookups returned: more than one
  suggests the plate moved between vehicles.
- **`dvla_match`** says whether the VES record describes the same vehicle as
  the DVSA record. A registration can move between vehicles, so a lookup can
  return another vehicle's record. Where at least two of make, year of
  manufacture and engine size disagree (`dvla_evidence`), the match is
  `different` and the pipeline does not use the record's values
  ([section 5.1](../../reports/methodology.md#dvsadvla-record-match)).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-dvla-status
#| tbl-cap: "Licensing status and DVLA lookup columns."
dict_table("dvla_status")
```

## Coverage

These columns have three levels of coverage, which apply to every `_DVLA`
column in the table:

1. **A lookup was made**: `r cov_pct(cs, "first_VES_check")` of vehicles. The
   lookup columns, such as `first_VES_check` and `is_error`, are present for
   all of these.
2. **The lookup returned a record**: `r cov_pct(cs, "first_VES_return")` of
   vehicles. The licensing status columns and the other `_DVLA` columns are
   present only for these.
3. **The record describes this vehicle**: `dvla_match` is `same` for
   `r fmt_pct(dm_n["same"] / sum(dm_n), 0)` of vehicles, `different` for
   `r fmt_pct(dm_n["different"] / sum(dm_n), 1)` and `no_dvla` for the rest.

How often a record was returned depends strongly on age (@fig-dd-dvla-status).
The VES only describes vehicles still on the DVLA register, so it returned a
record for `r cov_pct(cs, "first_VES_return", "Before 2000")` of vehicles
first used before 2000 and `r cov_pct(cs, "first_VES_return", "2000–09")` of
those first used in the 2000s, most of which have long left the road, against
`r cov_pct(cs, "first_VES_return", "2010–19")` of those first used in the
2010s. Where no record was returned, `error` holds the reason.

Vehicles first used in the last few years are a different case: many had not
been registered, or had not reached the DVSA data, when the lookups were made.
Hardly any vehicle first used in 2026 has a DVLA record
(`r cov_year("first_VES_return", 2026)`).

Some status fields are blank even where a record was returned, because the
DVLA holds no value: `taxDueDate_DVLA` for some vehicles that are not taxed, `motExpiryDate_DVLA` for vehicles too new to need an MOT, and
`artEndDate_DVLA` for all but the recent, expensive cars that pay the
additional rate of tax.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-dvla-status-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value, by year of first use."
coverage_table(cols)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dd-dvla-status
#| fig-cap: "Share of vehicles looked up in the VES, returned a record, and with a tax due date and MOT expiry date, by year of first use."
#| fig-height: 4.6
coverage_plot(c("first_VES_check", "first_VES_return", "taxDueDate_DVLA",
                "motExpiryDate_DVLA"))
```

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from 1990. Numeric columns and
dates show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and
maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each value, with the
less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing values as
*Blank*.

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(dict_values("dvla_status"))
```
